Point-like astronomical source

Words: 62
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
A point-like astronomical source has an angular extent negligible for the calculation or measurement being considered. The ideal mathematical limit concentrates its luminosity at one source-plane position. In gravitational lensing, this approximation permits divergent formal magnifications on a caustic; a finite source averages the magnification over its emitting area. An unresolved source need not have negligible size compared with the lens's caustic scale.

Parsec (pc)

Words: 29
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
A parsec is the distance corresponding to one arcsecond of annual parallax for a baseline of one astronomical unit. It is approximately 3.086×1016 metres. A megaparsec is one million parsecs.

Intergalactic medium (IGM)

Words: 497 Articles: 8
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
The intergalactic medium is the gas between galaxies. Its diffuse, ionized component contains much of the ordinary matter outside stars. Lyman-alpha absorption measures its small neutral-hydrogen fraction, while hotter phases require other tracers.

Temperature-density relation of photoionized intergalactic gas (T=T0​(1+δ)γ−1)

Words: 55
Intergalactic medium OurBigBook.com
Diffuse gas in photoionization equilibrium is often approximately described by the displayed temperature-density contrast relation. Photoheating and expansion cooling produce its thermal history. It is an empirical model for low-density gas, not the adiabatic equation of state of every intergalactic phase. Lyman-alpha forest line widths constrain both the temperature at a reference density and the slope through their lower envelope.

Cosmic ionizing background (Jν​)

Words: 35
Intergalactic medium OurBigBook.com
The cosmic ionizing background is the diffuse radiation field capable of photoionization of intergalactic gas. Its specific intensity depends on source luminosity functions, ionizing photon escape fractions, cosmological redshifting, and radiative transfer through absorbers. Quasars and star formation supply major contributions with different spectral shapes and evolution.

Lyman-alpha forest

Words: 376 Articles: 5
Intergalactic medium OurBigBook.com
The Lyman-alpha forest is the collection of foreground Lyman-alpha absorption features in a distant quasar spectrum. Each observed wavelength identifies a cosmological redshift. Weak forest lines usually sample diffuse intergalactic medium at modest density contrast; strong, self-shielding absorbers need a different density interpretation.

Lyman-alpha forest photoionization scaling (nHI​≃α(T)nH2​/Γ)

Words: 128 Articles: 1
Lyman-alpha forest OurBigBook.com
In optically thin, almost fully ionized hydrogen in photoionization equilibrium, nHI​Γ=ne​np​α(T) and ne​≃np​≃nH​. Thus the neutral fraction is approximately α(T)nH​/Γ, while the neutral density is proportional to nH2​. At fixed overdensity, cosmic dilution gives nH​∝(1+z)3, hence nHI​∝α(T)(1+z)6/Γ. Gas density, temperature, ionizing radiation and path length are all required to infer a baryon density from Lyman-alpha absorption.
Jeans-length ionization correction for the Lyman-alpha forest (NH​∝NHI1/3​Γ1/3[fg​T/α(T)]1/3)
Words: 66
Lyman-alpha forest photoionization scaling OurBigBook.com
Assume optically thin photoionization equilibrium and an absorber depth of order its local Jeans length, L∝(fg​T/nH​)1/2, where fg​ is the local gas fraction. Then NHI​≃α(T)nH2​L/Γ∝[α(T)/Γ](fg​T)1/2nH3/2​. Solving for nH​ and substituting in NH​=nH​L gives the displayed correction. Thus the ionized mass integral weights the neutral-hydrogen column-density distribution by NHI1/3​ rather than NHI​. This model does not apply without modification to optically thick systems or arbitrary unconfined gas.

Redshift evolution of the Lyman-alpha forest

Words: 73
Lyman-alpha forest OurBigBook.com
The Lyman-alpha forest becomes denser and more opaque towards higher cosmological redshift, for a fixed absorption selection over the ordinary post-reionization range. The incidence is often parametrized as dN/dz=A(1+z)γ, with the index depending on the column density threshold and epoch. The evolution flattens at low redshift as the declining cosmic ionizing background partly offsets dilution of the intergalactic medium. For optically thin gas at fixed overdensity, photoionization equilibrium gives approximately nHI​∝α(T)(1+z)6/Γ, illustrating why density, temperature and ionizing radiation all matter.

Proximity effect (astrophysics)

Words: 139 Articles: 1
Lyman-alpha forest OurBigBook.com
The quasar proximity effect is a reduction of nearby Lyman-alpha forest absorption caused by extra photoionization from the quasar. At fixed density and temperature in photoionization equilibrium, an added rate ΓQ​ changes the neutral fraction by the factor Γbg​/(Γbg​+ΓQ​). A host environment with positive density contrast can mask this reduction, and a variable or anisotropic source complicates its interpretation.
Proximity-effect estimator of the ionizing background (NHI​=NHI(0)​/(1+ω),ω=ΓQ​/Γbg​)
Words: 83
Proximity effect (astrophysics) OurBigBook.com
In photoionization equilibrium at fixed gas density and temperature, the extra quasar photoionization rate reduces neutral-hydrogen column density by the displayed factor. Its local rate is calculated from the quasar flux, while the isotropic background rate is Γbg​=4π∫Jν​σHI​(ν)/(hν)dν. Fitting the absorption suppression versus proper distance constrains the cosmic ionizing background. For an unperturbed column-density distribution proportional to N−p with p>1, the line abundance above a fixed threshold is reduced by (1+ω)1−p. Density enhancement, quasar age, anisotropy and redshift errors must be distinguished from this ionization effect.

Photoevaporation

Words: 283 Articles: 4
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
Radiation heats gas sufficiently to drive an escaping thermal outflow. It can remove material from protoplanetary disks, planetary atmospheres and irradiated clouds. In a heated Keplerian disk, the photoevaporative gravitational radius compares the sound speed with the orbital speed. The mass-loss rate depends on the heating, density and wind geometry rather than radiation pressure alone.

Photoevaporative gap opening

Words: 53
Photoevaporation OurBigBook.com
When a protoplanetary disk's inward viscous supply approaches its wind-loss rate, photoevaporation can prevent replenishment of the inner disk. That region drains on a viscous timescale, leaving a gap or hole. A negative density in a formal steady state calculation signals the breakdown of that approximation, not a physical continuation. An exposed outer edge can subsequently disperse rapidly.

Steady photoevaporating-disk mass flux (Facc​=M˙d​−M˙w​rg​/r​)

Words: 114 Articles: 1
Photoevaporation OurBigBook.com
For a sink W=W0​(r/rg​)−5/2 outside rg​, mass conservation gives dFacc​/dr=2πrW in steady state. Remote feeding gives Facc​=M˙d​−M˙w​ inside rg​, and M˙d​−M˙w​rg​/r​ outside, where M˙w​=4πW0​rg2​. The inward flux decreases towards the star because mass is diverted into the wind. A finite feeding radius or outer truncation supplies an additional boundary condition.

Surface density of a steady photoevaporating disk (3πνΣ=M˙d​−M˙w​rg​/r​[1+21​log(r/rg​)])

Words: 57
Steady photoevaporating-disk mass flux OurBigBook.com
With constant kinematic viscosity and zero inner viscous torque in an accretion disk, νΣr​=(6π)−1∫0r​Facc​(r′)/r′​dr′. For the steady photoevaporating-disk mass flux, the density is (M˙d​−M˙w​)/(3πν) inside rg​ and the displayed logarithmic profile outside. At equal feeding and wind rates the inner density vanishes, and the outer normalized profile rises from zero with zero slope and tends to one. Its near-edge expansion is (r/rg​−1)2/8.

Photoevaporative gravitational radius (rg​=GM/cs2​)

Words: 68
Photoevaporation OurBigBook.com
The thermal binding scale defined by equating heated gas sound speed to circular Keplerian orbit speed. It is rg​=GM/cs2​. The circular-orbit binding energy is GM/(2r) per unit mass, while the gas specific enthalpy is of order cs2​. A heated disk surface at radii comparable to or larger than rg​ can therefore drive photoevaporation. The actual launching radius can differ by a factor of order unity; cs​ is not the ballistic escape speed.

Gravitational collapse

Words: 338 Articles: 4
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
Gravitational collapse is contraction driven by a system's own gravitational attraction or an enclosing potential. Pressure, angular momentum and other stresses can oppose it. A free-fall timescale measures the dynamical contraction rate when pressure support is removed; gas cooling determines whether thermal support can be removed fast enough.

Pressureless homologous spherical collapse (R2R¨=−GM)

Words: 237 Articles: 2
Gravitational collapse OurBigBook.com
A uniform spherical cloud with negligible pressure and velocity u=(R˙/R)r remains uniform: the continuity equation gives ρR3=ρ00​R03​. The shell theorem gives interior gravitational acceleration −(4πGρ/3)r, so its outer radius satisfies the displayed equation, with fixed mass M=4πρ00​R03​/3. Collapse from rest has R˙2=2GM(1/R−1/R0​). Writing C2=2GM/R0​, its cycloid parametrization is R=R0​(1+cosϕ)/2 and Ct=R0​(ϕ+sinϕ)/2, for 0≤ϕ≤π. Complete collapse occurs after 3π/(32Gρ00​)​. This Newtonian dust solution ceases to be a regular fluid configuration at zero radius.

Comoving perturbations of a homologously collapsing cloud (k(t)=q/R(t))

Words: 159 Articles: 1
Pressureless homologous spherical collapse OurBigBook.com
A Fourier mode advected with a homologous spherical flow has phase q⋅r/R(t). Its material derivative in the background vanishes because k˙=−(R˙/R)k. Thus contraction shortens its physical wavelength while preserving its phase on each fluid element. Linearizing the continuity equation and pressureless momentum equation gives δ˙=−ik⋅u1​ and u˙1​+(R˙/R)u1​=−ikΦ1​. Combining these with the Poisson equation for Newtonian gravity yields δ¨+2(R˙/R)δ˙−4πGρδ=0 for nonzero compressive wavenumber. It is a local bulk calculation, without the moving cloud-boundary conditions.
Density modes of a collapsing pressureless sphere (δg​∼R−3/2,δd​∼R)
Words: 85
Comoving perturbations of a homologously collapsing cloud OurBigBook.com
For pressureless homologous spherical collapse, let ϕ be its cycloid parameter. The density contrast equation becomes δϕϕ​−tan(ϕ/2)δϕ​−3δ/(1+cosϕ)=0. One solution is δg​=sinϕ/(1+cosϕ)2. Reduction of order gives an independent solution that decays at collapse,
δd​=δg​∫ϕπ​sin2s(1+coss)3​ds=δg​[4cot(ϕ/2)+sinϕ−3(π−ϕ)].
(1)
For ϵ=π−ϕ, the integral is ϵ5/40+O(ϵ7), while δg​∼4ϵ−3. Therefore δd​∼ϵ2/10. Since R∼R0​ϵ2/4, the displayed powers follow. The growing branch is unique up to scale and addition of the decaying branch; many mixed solutions grow, so it is not literally the only function with growth. Finite perturbations eventually leave the linear regime.

Free-fall time of a uniform sphere (tff​=3π/(32Gρ)​)

Words: 55
Gravitational collapse OurBigBook.com
A pressureless uniform sphere initially at rest collapses under Newtonian gravity in a time depending only on its initial mass density. Solving the radial shell equation gives 3π/(32Gρ)​. It is commonly used as a dynamical-time benchmark for cooling and star formation, with the gravitating density rather than gas density alone when other matter supplies gravity.

A colour index is the difference of an object's measured apparent magnitudes in two photometric passbands, such as B−V. The traditional near- and thermal-infrared photometric bands in the 1–5 micrometre region are J,H,K,L,M, with approximate centers 1.25,1.65,2.2,3.5,4.8 micrometres. Variants such as Ks​, L′ and M′ have different detailed responses. They largely follow atmospheric windows; transmission, sky brightness, and detector response determine practical band edges. The K-correction converts an observed photometric passband to a specified emitted photometric passband, accounting for cosmological redshift and the source spectrum. For a narrow same-band measurement, KR​=−2.5log10​[(1+z)Lν​((1+z)νR​)/Lν​(νR​)]. Thus its sign depends on the spectrum, not on redshift alone. For Lν​∝να, it is −2.5(1+α)log10​(1+z). For emitted spectral power per steradian Pν​∝ν−α, the luminosity distance gives Sνo​​=(1+z)P(1+z)νo​​/dL2​. Photon energy and arrival-rate redshifts supply two factors of 1+z, while the observed frequency interval is reduced by one. Substitution of the power-law spectrum gives the displayed K correction. This convention uses spectral flux per unit frequency and power per steradian; using per unit wavelength or total spectral luminosity changes the corresponding factors.

The Gaunt factor is the dimensionless quantum correction to a classical free-free radiation calculation. Its weak temperature and frequency dependence modifies the approximate thermal bremsstrahlung scaling; a frequency-averaged value appears in the bolometric cooling coefficient.

Radiative transfer OurBigBook.com
Specific intensity is power per projected area, solid angle, and frequency interval. In vacuum it is conserved along a ray.

Vacuum conservation of specific intensity

Words: 66
Specific intensity OurBigBook.com
In a transparent, stationary Euclidean vacuum, the radiative transfer equation has zero absorption and emission, so dIν​/ds=0. Equivalently, two surface elements exchange beam power Iν​cosθ1​cosθ2​dA1​dA2​dν/s2; reversing the description of the same beam cancels its geometric factors. The observed radiative flux of an unresolved source still falls as its apparent solid angle, proportional to s−2. Across gravitational or cosmological frequency shifts the invariant is Iν​/ν3, not generally Iν​.

Specific intensity OurBigBook.com
Limb darkening is the decrease of emergent specific intensity toward the apparent edge of a stellar disc. A transit depth then depends on the intensity sampled by the planet as well as its projected area; the uniform-disc area ratio is only an approximation.

Optical depth satisfies dτν​=αν​ds along a path and measures attenuation through Iν​∝e−τν​ in the absence of emission.

Optical depth OurBigBook.com
An optically thick medium has optical depth τ≫1 along the relevant path. Photons undergo many interactions before escaping. Radiative diffusion applies under suitable near-isotropy conditions, but a large scattering depth alone does not guarantee thermalization when true absorption is weak.

Optical depth OurBigBook.com
An optically thin medium has τ≪1, so attenuation and emission may be expanded to first order in optical depth.

Optically thin medium OurBigBook.com
For isotropic emission without significant absorption, integrating the spontaneous photon-production rate along the sightline gives the displayed energy intensity per solid angle. Photon intensity omits the factor hν. Summing unresolved transitions is necessary before comparing with an observed blended spectral feature.

A collision or transient molecular pair can possess a dipole even when the isolated molecules do not. The resulting opacity can be important in a dense molecular hydrogen atmosphere. Pair absorption per unit length scales approximately as the product of the two partner number densities, so its mass absorption coefficient is generally density-dependent. It supplies continuum absorption between ordinary spectral lines.

For isothermal optically thin dust at distance D, its measured spectral flux density determines its mass through Md​=Fν​D2/[κν​Bν​(T)]. Temperature and opacity uncertainty commonly dominate the inferred mass uncertainty.

μdτν​dIν​​=Iν​−Sν​,

The radiative transfer source function is emission per unit extinction. If jν​ is emission per unit path length and ρκν​ is extinction per unit path length, Sν​=jν​/(ρκν​) and the transfer equation is μ∂τν​​Iν​=Iν​−Sν​. Under thermal absorption in local thermodynamic equilibrium it is the Planck function; for conservative coherent isotropic scattering it is the mean intensity.

Radiative diffusion OurBigBook.com
The Rosseland mean opacity is the harmonic frequency average weighted by ∂Bν​/∂T. It controls radiative diffusion because flux preferentially travels through low-opacity frequencies.
It is a frequency-averaged opacity appropriate to the radiative-diffusion limit, not the general opacity concept itself.

In local thermodynamic equilibrium, matter populations are thermal at the local temperature and the source function is the Planck function, Sν​=Bν​(T).

Iν​(0,μ)=Iν​(τb​,μ)e−τb​/μ+∫0τb​​Bν​[T(t)]e−t/μμdt​.

Along a radial ray through a layer with constant source function, the incident specific intensity is attenuated by e−τ and the layer adds S(1−e−τ). At small optical depth, Iout​=Iin​+(S−Iin​)τ+O(τ2). Whether the source exceeds the incident specific intensity determines the first-order emission or absorption contrast.

Formal solution of the radiative transfer equation OurBigBook.com
For a semi-infinite plane-parallel atmosphere with polynomial source function S(τ)=∑aj​τj, the outward specific intensity is ∫0∞​S(τ)e−τ/μdτ/μ. Substitution u=τ/μ gives coefficients Aj​=j!aj​ in the surface polynomial in μ. The deep boundary term must vanish. A local truncated Taylor series instead gives this contribution plus a remainder, so its surface polynomial is not automatically exact.

Words: 54
Formal solution of the radiative transfer equation OurBigBook.com
For a thermalized radiative transfer source function Sλ​=Bλ​(T) constant along a ray, the specific intensity after optical-depth interval Δτ is Iλ​=Bλ​+(Iin​−Bλ​)e−Δτ/μ for μ>0. As Δτ→∞, it tends to the Planck function, independently of a bounded boundary input. A temperature gradient is unnecessary for blackbody emission. One-layer spectral contrast
Words: 76
Formal solution of the radiative transfer equation OurBigBook.com
A non-scattering isothermal atmospheric layer in local thermodynamic equilibrium, of temperature Ta​ and slant optical depth tλ​, lies above a blackbody background at Tb​. The specific intensity is
Iλ​=Bλ​(Tb​)e−tλ​+Bλ​(Ta​)(1−e−tλ​).
(11)
Thus an increase in opacity shifts the specific intensity toward the layer's Planck function. If a line is more opaque than its continuum, it appears in absorption for Ta​<Tb​, in emission for Ta​>Tb​, and has no contrast for Ta​=Tb​. This is a local explanation, not a claim that all features diagnose one uniform layer.

Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
A fixed-mass shell with ultraviolet opacity κUV​ has dust transparency radius RUV​=κUV​Msh​/(4π)​. For an initially expanding shell driven by constant ultraviolet luminosity, a sharp opaque-to-transparent approximation gives
v∞2​=v02​+R0​2GM​[Γss​(2X−1)+ΓIR​(1−X−1)−1],X=RUV​/R0​.
(43)
Here Γss​=LR02​/(GMMsh​c) is the initial single-scattering force ratio and ΓIR​=κIR​L/(4πGMc). The trajectory must actually reach RUV​. Large initial ultraviolet optical depth enhances the radiative work at fixed initial single-scattering ratio; the same conclusion does not follow unconditionally at fixed electron-scattering luminosity.
Critical luminosity of a dusty shell (Lcrit​)
Words: 36
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
The critical luminosity of a dusty shell is the luminosity at which radiation pressure balances gravity. For shell mass Ms​, enclosed gravitating mass M, and ultraviolet and infrared optical depths,
Lcrit​=r2(1+τIR​−e−τUV​)GcMMs​​.
(44)
Thin-shell momentum equation
Words: 38
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
For a spherical swept shell of mass Ms​(R), radial speed R˙, driving force Fd​, and enclosed gravitating mass M(<R),
dtd​[Ms​(R)R˙]=Fd​−R2GMs​(R)M(<R)​.
(45)
The derivative includes momentum needed to accelerate newly swept ambient mass.
Dust transparency radius (Rτ​)
Words: 28
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
The dust transparency radius is where a swept shell's ultraviolet optical depth equals one. For a gas fraction fg​ in a singular isothermal sphere, Rτ​=κUV​fg​σ2/(2πG).

Soltan argument

Words: 33
Supermassive black hole OurBigBook.com
The Soltan argument compares the cosmological energy density radiated by active galactic nuclei with the present mass density in supermassive black holes. Their ratio constrains the mass-weighted mean radiative efficiency of black-hole growth.

Tidal disruption event (TDE)

Words: 101 Articles: 2
Astrophysical black hole OurBigBook.com
A tidal disruption event occurs when a star passes close enough to a black hole that differential gravity tears it apart outside the capture boundary, producing returning debris and often a luminous flare.

Tidal disruption radius (rt​)

Words: 32
Tidal disruption event OurBigBook.com
For a star of mass M∗​ and radius R∗​ near a black hole of mass MBH​, the Newtonian tidal disruption radius is rt​≃R∗​(2MBH​/M∗​)1/3 under a peak-to-center tidal-acceleration convention.

Hills mass

Words: 36
Tidal disruption event OurBigBook.com
The Hills mass is the black-hole mass above which a given star crosses the capture boundary before being tidally disrupted. For a Schwarzschild capture radius 2GMBH​/c2, it is c3R∗3/2​/(2G3/2M∗1/2​) with the corresponding tidal-radius convention.

Black-hole seed

Words: 113 Articles: 3
Astrophysical black hole OurBigBook.com
A black-hole seed is an early black hole from which a later massive black hole can grow by accretion and mergers.

Population III remnant black-hole seed

Words: 30
Black-hole seed OurBigBook.com
A Population III remnant seed forms when a massive metal-free star collapses, typically leaving a light seed of order 10--102M⊙​ depending on stellar mass loss and pair-instability effects.

Runaway stellar-collision black-hole seed

Words: 33
Black-hole seed OurBigBook.com
A runaway stellar-collision seed forms when mass segregation and repeated mergers in a dense young cluster create a very massive star that collapses to a black hole of roughly 102--104M⊙​.

Direct-collapse black-hole seed (DCBH seed)

Words: 29
Black-hole seed OurBigBook.com
A direct-collapse black-hole seed forms when rapidly inflowing primordial gas avoids fragmentation, builds a supermassive star or quasistar, and collapses to a seed of roughly 104--106M⊙​.

Observational astronomy

Words: 375 Articles: 8
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com

Flux-limited galaxy selection (Vmax​∝L3/2)

Words: 69
Observational astronomy OurBigBook.com
For a nearby Euclidean survey with limiting flux fmin​, a galaxy of luminosity L is detectable out to dmax​=L/(4πfmin​)​. Its accessible volume is therefore proportional to L3/2. With a Schechter function ϕ(L)∝Lαe−L/L∗​, counts per logarithmic interval are proportional to Lα+5/2e−L/L∗​ and peak at (α+5/2)L∗​ when α>−5/2. This selection suppresses faint objects relative to a volume-limited census; finite survey boundaries and cosmological evolution modify the simple law.

Angular resolution (θres​)

Words: 44
Observational astronomy OurBigBook.com
Angular resolution describes the smallest angular separation or structure an observation can distinguish. A physical scale r at distance D subtends approximately r/D radians when r≪D. Resolving a black-hole sphere of influence therefore involves distance as well as its physical radius, and useful kinematics also require adequate surface brightness.

Surface brightness (I)

Words: 139 Articles: 2
Observational astronomy OurBigBook.com
Surface brightness is received flux per unit solid angle on the sky. It describes the brightness of an extended source independently of a particular aperture's area. An isophote is a contour of constant surface brightness; central surface brightness sets the available photons for resolved galaxy spectroscopy.

Sérsic profile (I(R)=Ie​e−bn​[(R/Re​)1/n−1])

Words: 49
Surface brightness OurBigBook.com
A Sérsic profile models projected galactic light, with index n controlling curvature and bn​ chosen so that Re​ encloses half the luminosity. Its logarithmic slope is dlnI/dlnR=−(bn​/n)(R/Re​)1/n. The n=1 case is exponential; n=4 gives the traditional de Vaucouleurs form. Unlike a fixed power law, its slope steepens outward.

Projection of a spherical power-law emissivity (j∝r−p⟹I∝R1−p)

Words: 50
Surface brightness OurBigBook.com
An optically thin spherical source with volume emissivity j(r)=j0​r−p has surface brightness
I(R)=4πj0​​R1−pπ​Γ(p/2)Γ((p−1)/2)​,p>1.
(46)
Substitute z=Ru in the line-of-sight integral and evaluate ∫−∞∞​(1+u2)−p/2du using the beta function. The condition p>1 is convergence at large distance. A core or finite outer boundary changes the projection near that boundary; the stated scaling applies between those scales.

Isophote

Words: 90 Articles: 1
Observational astronomy OurBigBook.com
An isophote is a contour of equal surface brightness in an astronomical image. Deviations from fitted ellipses encode additional information about a galaxy's projected stellar structure.

Boxy and disky isophotes (a4​cos(4θ))

Words: 65
Isophote OurBigBook.com
Writing an isophote's radial residual about its fitted ellipse as δr=a4​cos4θ+⋯, positive a4​ extends the major and minor axes and gives a pointed, disky shape; negative a4​ extends diagonal directions and gives a boxy shape. The sign stated here is for radial residuals, not an unconverted brightness residual. Massive slowly rotating elliptical galaxies commonly have boxy isophotes, while embedded rotating disks commonly make lower-mass elliptical galaxies disky.

Sky brightness

Words: 33
Observational astronomy OurBigBook.com
Sky brightness is the diffuse radiance received away from an astronomical target. Ground-based observations include atmospheric airglow, scattered light, and thermal radiation; extraterrestrial diffuse light also contributes. Its photon fluctuations contribute to the signal-to-noise ratio in photon counting.
